Here’s a highly advanced Keras + TensorFlow project—far beyond standard CNN/RNN work—focused on Neural Architecture Search (NAS) for object detection, utilizing EfficientDet-style compound scaling. This leverages keras_tuner for automatic architecture exploration.

🧠 Project Title

ai-ml-ds-QpLmZ8xCvBn: Auto‑Scaled Object Detector via NAS
Filename: auto_scaled_detector_nas.py

Short Description:
Automatically searches and tunes a mobile-friendly object detector architecture, scaling depth, width, resolution, and FPN levels. You’ll build a Keras/TensorFlow end-to-end pipeline—from data loading and augmentation to NAS-based model optimization—resulting in an EfficientDet-inspired detector tuned for your use-case.

# auto_scaled_detector_nas.py

import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
import tensorflow_datasets as tfds
import kerastuner

# HyperModel defining EfficientDet-like components
class EfficientDetNAS(kerastuner.HyperModel):
    def __init__(self, num_classes: int):
        self.num_classes: int = num_classes

    def build(self, hp: kerastuner.HyperParameters) -> tf.keras.Model:
        # Compound scaling: depth, width, resolution factors
        depth_coef: int = hp.Int("depth", 1, 5)
        width_coef: float = hp.Float("width", 0.5, 2.0, step=0.25)
        base_res: int = hp.Choice("res", [128, 256, 512])

        inputs: tf.Tensor = layers.Input(shape=(base_res, base_res, 3))
        x: tf.Tensor = inputs

        # Backbone: scaled MobileNetV3
        backbone = keras.applications.MobileNetV3Small(
            include_top=False,
            input_tensor=inputs,
            alpha=width_coef,
            weights=None,
        )
        x = backbone.output

        # BiFPN layers for feature fusion
        for i in range(depth_coef):
            x = layers.Conv2D(int(64 * width_coef), 3, padding='same', activation='relu')(x)
            x = layers.BatchNormalization()(x)

        # Prediction heads
        cls_out = layers.Conv2D(self.num_classes, kernel_size=3, padding='same', activation='sigmoid', name="class_out")(x)
        box_out = layers.Conv2D(4, kernel_size=3, padding='same', name="box_out")(x)

        model: tf.keras.Model = keras.Model(inputs=inputs, outputs=[cls_out, box_out])
        model.compile(
            optimizer="adam",
            loss={"class_out": "categorical_crossentropy", "box_out": "mse"},
            metrics={"class_out": "accuracy"}
        )
        return model

# Load and preprocess COCO subset
def prepare_dataset(res: int, batch: int = 8):
    def preprocess(sample):
        img: tf.Tensor = tf.image.resize(sample["image"], (res, res)) / 255.0
        cls = tf.one_hot(sample["objects"]["label"][0], depth=80)
        bbox = sample["objects"]["bbox"][0]
        return img, {"class_out": cls, "box_out": bbox}
    ds: tf.data.Dataset = tfds.load("coco/2017", split="train[:5%]", shuffle_files=True)
    ds = ds.map(preprocess, num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE).batch(batch).prefetch(tf.data.AUTOTUNE)
    return ds

# Search over architecture
num_classes: int = 80
tuner = kerastuner.RandomSearch(
    EfficientDetNAS(num_classes),
    objective="val_class_out_accuracy",
    max_trials=10,
    executions_per_trial=1,
    directory="nas_effdet",
    project_name="auto_effdet"
)

# Run NAS
tuner.search_space_summary()
# You can vary resolution later
train_ds = prepare_dataset(res=256)
val_ds = prepare_dataset(res=256)
tuner.search(train_ds, validation_data=val_ds, epochs=5)

# Retrieve best model
best: tf.keras.Model = tuner.get_best_models(num_models=1)[0]
best.save("best_effdet_nas.h5")

🔍 Example Use Case & Expected Output

Use Case:
Train and evaluate a tuned EfficientDet-style model on a 5% subset of COCO 2017.

# After running tuner
model = tf.keras.models.load_model("best_effdet_nas.h5")
img: np.ndarray = np.random.rand(1,256,256,3).astype(np.float32)
cls_map, bbox = model.predict(img)
# cls_map: (1,256,256,80), bbox: (1,256,256,4)

Expect accurate localization and classification maps fine‑tuned via NAS.

🚀 Key Learnings

  • Components: MobileNetV3 backbone, BiFPN-like convolutions, compound scaling
  • Keywords: Neural Architecture Search, EfficientDet, compound scaling, object detection
  • Research Areas: NAS for detection, resource-aware architecture search, BiFPN
  • Hashtags/Googleables: #EfficientDetNAS #CompoundScaling #TFObjectDetection #NASinKeras

🏭 Problem Domain

Object detection optimization through NAS, catering to mobile/embedded constraints for real-time inference.

Use Cases

  • Custom mobile object detection (drones, robotics)
  • Optimized architecture discovery for industrial inspection
  • Edge device deployment with size/performance trade-offs

🧱 Frameworks

  • TensorFlow 2.x + Keras
  • Keras Tuner NAS
  • TensorFlow Datasets (COCO subset)

🗂 Development Lifecycle

  1. Define optimization goals & constraints
  2. Data pipeline with augmentation
  3. NAS search setup (search space definition)
  4. Training & validation
  5. Architect selection and export
  6. Edge/cloud integration (TFLite / TF Serving)
  7. Monitoring (latency, accuracy)
  8. Future retraining iterations

🤝 Sister Projects

  • Transformer-based detectors (DETR)
  • Quantization-aware NAS
  • NAS for segmentation (e.g. U-Net)

🔗 Integrations

  • TF Lite for mobile/edge
  • TensorFlow Serving
  • OpenCV / RTSP for real-time capture
  • Model hub for versioning

⏱ Timestamp

2025-07-15

⏳ Completion Timeframe

6–8 weeks end-to-end, including tuning and edge deployment.

🎯 Final Output

A NAS‑optimized object detector with best trade-offs; outputs per-pixel detection maps and bounding boxes, packaged for low-latency serving or TFLite deployment.

💡 Bonus Challenge

Integrate quantization-aware training (QAT) during NAS to directly obtain integer-based models. Further, introduce an attention-based BiFPN variant and search across different FPN depths.

🔭 Next Steps

  • Scale to full COCO or custom datasets
  • Integrate AutoML for QAT pruning
  • Blend with transformer backbones (ViT + FPN)
  • Build an end-to‑end deployment pipeline with CI/CD, performance metrics, A/B comparisons

This project truly escalates complexity—blending NAS, object detection, scalable design, and deployment readiness. Let’s push boundaries!
